maya: Kicking off canary for monarch16b-int4. quick note: getting OOMs on some long gens, likely fragmentation + prefetch interaction.
raj: paste the pod log?
maya: from pod m-2:
```
E2026-03-18 14:02:03.112 | cuda: malloc failed (out of memory) size=1.5GB
I2026-03-18 14:02:03.113 | kv_slots=48, kv_resident=1.9G, frag=19%
I2026-03-18 14:02:03.114 | req: batch=1, user_len=400, max_new_tokens=400
```
elin: 19% frag with those kv_slots screams int4 packing inefficiency — we saw the same with orbis30b. prefetch reserves contiguous scratch which pushes fragmentation higher
sasha: bench numbers from local run:
- monarch16b-int4 (prefetch ON, max_new=256): 540 tok/s, 2.1% instr-follow drop vs fp16
- monarch16b-int4 (prefetch OFF, max_new=128): 610 tok/s, 1.0% drop
- monarch16b-mixed (attn weights int8, rest int4): 580 tok/s, 0.4% drop
raj: interesting. so disabling prefetch gives better throughput in that config?
sasha: yes for this model. turnover of allocations is lower so compactor can keep up. prefetch helped elsewhere but not here
tomas: short-term mitigation I can push: runtime will detect frag>15% and reply with a soft-guard that forces microbatch=1 and suggests `max_new_tokens=128` in the response metadata. PR in review: https://git.internal/r/rt/frag-safeguard
maya: can we also flip slot compactor to `aggressive` for the canary pods?
tomas: yes. will add env flag `SLOT_COMPACTOR=aggressive` to canary deployment
raj: docs change: update model page to call out `monarch16b-int4 defaults: max_new_tokens=128, prefetch=false, compactor=aggressive`. also add note about per-channel calibration for quality
elin: on quality: ran a per-channel symmetric scale sweep on the attention heads. recovered ~1.1 pts out of the 2.1 drop on the instr-follow set when applied to query/key projections only
maya: nice. can you upload the tuned scales to S3 and give a hash? we can mount as a runtime override
sasha: uploaded to s3://redwood-models/monarch/monarch16b-int4-calibrated-v1.tar.gz (sha256: b3f2a9f4...). weights are ~1.2GB
raj: what about cost math? tokens/sec vs nebula20b baseline?
sasha: quick cost proxy: monarch int4 (post-cal) = 600 tok/s, nebula20b-quant = 420 tok/s. rough serving cost reduction ~28% per-token for monarch in int4 vs nebula20b on same infra profile
maya: infra-bot queued a canary deploy with flags: prefetch=false, compactor=aggressive, max_new_default=128, mount-scale=s3://...
infra-bot: deploy queued for `monarch-int4-canary` image v1.3.4 — 4 pods target
deploy-bot: canary started at 14:10 — logs + metrics at https://grafana.internal/redwood/monarch-canary
tomas: reminder: runtime safegate only kicks in when frag>15% AND request.max_new_tokens>200. reduces noisy tripping for smaller gens
raj: action items:
- maya: run 48h canary with eval hooks (summarization + instr-follow + latency tail)
- sasha: provide calibrated weights manifest + brief on calibration method
- tomas: finish runtime safegate PR and add telemetry for safegate hits
- raj: draft release note blurb + model page defaults update
maya: i'll post canary link and first 6h metrics here. thanks all :thumbsup:
